references.shows: Mamadou Kouyaté's 21-string kora shows the long neck with braided leather tuning collars, calabash, paired handles, and tall bridge.
The neutral museum photograph shows the hide fasteners, hemispherical calabash and its proportions relative to the neck. Several strings are missing.
A stringing demonstration explains and illustrates how strings pass through notches on both sides of the bridge and onto leather neck collars.

silhouette: An upright three-quarter view, with a long neck above the skin-covered gourd, a tall projecting bridge and a pair of wooden handgrips framing the string fan.
features: Hemispherical gourd resonator with a plain skin face
Long neck with leather tuning collars and a tail anchor below the resonator
Tall notched bridge projecting from a pad on the skin face
Twenty-one fine strings grouped into two ordered banks of eleven and ten
Two distinct upper ends of the parallel handgrips rising past the gourd
iconFeatures: Upright playing position with a round calabash at the bottom of a long neck
Projecting bridge and open triangular string silhouette
avoid: A neck lying across the canvas in the pose of a guitar
All strings converging on a single point on the bridge
Frets or guitar-style tuning keys on this leather-collar model
notes: Shows a traditional 21-string Mandinka kora with sliding leather collars. Fine strings and a plain skin face keep the bridge, grips and gourd readable at a glance.

geometry.proportions: A long narrow neck projects well above a wide round gourd.
geometry.partLayout: Two banks of eleven and ten strings meet opposite sides of the projecting bridge. Twin handgrips rise from the skin on either side.

documentedDimensions.value: 115.8 cm tall × 52.5 cm wide, about 2.2:1 overall
